question: Which transparent, curved front part of the eye refracts light rays entering the eye most strongly?
options: Iris / 虹膜
Cornea / 角膜
Sclera / 鞏膜
Choroid / 脈絡膜

question: What is the function of the choroid (脈絡膜) in the human eye?
options: To detect colour under bright light
To absorb excess light to prevent internal reflection and supply nutrients and oxygen to the retina via blood vessels
To adjust the curvature of the lens
To secrete tears to keep the cornea moist

question: In bright light, the circular muscles of the iris contract while the radial muscles relax, constricting the pupil to reduce the amount of light entering the eye.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: How does the eye focus on a near object during accommodation (視覺調節)?
options: Ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments tighten, and the lens becomes thinner.
Ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken, and the elastic lens becomes thicker and more convex.
Radial muscles of the iris contract to widen the pupil.
The eyeball elongates backward toward the optic nerve.

question: Which type of photoreceptor on the retina is responsible for colour vision and high visual acuity in bright light?
options: Rod cells / 視桿細胞
Cone cells / 視錐細胞
Bipolar neurones / 雙極神經元
Ganglion cells / 神經節細胞

question: The yellow spot (fovea / 黃點) contains a very high density of cone cells and no rod cells, providing the sharpest colour vision when light focuses directly on it.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Why is there a blind spot (盲點) on the retina?
options: It is covered by a thick layer of dark pigment.
It is the region where nerve fibres leave the eyeball to form the optic nerve, so no photoreceptors are present there.
It contains only rod cells that cannot detect bright light.
It is blocked by the ciliary body.

question: What causes short-sightedness (myopia / 近視) and how is it corrected?
options: The eyeball is too short or the lens is too thin; corrected with a convex lens.
The eyeball is too long or the lens is too thick, causing distant light rays to focus in front of the retina; corrected with a concave (diverging) lens.
The cornea has an uneven curvature; corrected with a cylindrical lens.
The optic nerve is damaged; corrected with eye drops.

question: Long-sightedness (hypermetropia / 遠視) occurs when light rays from near objects focus behind the retina and is corrected using a convex (converging) lens.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which three ear ossicles (聽小骨) transmit and amplify vibrations from the eardrum across the middle ear to the oval window?
options: Pinna, auditory canal, and Eustachian tube
Hammer (malleus), anvil (incus), and stirrup (stapes) / 錘骨、砧骨、鐙骨
Cochlea, semicircular canals, and round window
Retina, choroid, and sclera

question: What is the function of the Eustachian tube (耳咽管) connecting the middle ear to the pharynx?
options: To amplify sound waves before they reach the cochlea
To equalize air pressure on both sides of the eardrum so it can vibrate freely without damage
To drain endolymph from the semicircular canals
To detect rotational movements of the head

question: Sensory hair cells inside the cochlea (耳蝸) detect pressure vibrations in the fluid (endolymph) and generate nerve impulses sent to the brain via the auditory nerve.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: What is the role of the round window (圓窗) in the inner ear?
options: To collect sound waves from the outside air
To bulge outward and release fluid pressure in the cochlea after vibrations pass through
To secrete earwax in the auditory canal
To connect the stirrup to the eardrum

question: Which structures in the inner ear detect head rotation and help maintain body balance?
options: Cochlea and Eustachian tube
Semicircular canals (半規管) arranged in three planes at right angles to one another
Eardrum and ear ossicles
Pinna and auditory canal

question: Phototropism (向光性) is the directional growth movement of a plant part in response to unilateral light.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: How does unilateral light cause a plant shoot tip (coleoptile) to bend toward the light source?
options: Auxins accumulate on the illuminated side and inhibit cell elongation there.
Auxins migrate from the illuminated side to the shaded side, stimulating faster cell elongation on the shaded side.
Light destroys all cells on the shaded side.
Chloroplasts pull the stem toward the sun.

question: In Darwin's and Boysen-Jensen's classic experiments on oat coleoptiles, what happens when a mica plate (impermeable to chemicals) is inserted horizontally just below the tip on the shaded side?
options: The coleoptile bends strongly toward the light.
The coleoptile does not bend because auxins produced at the tip cannot diffuse down the shaded side.
The coleoptile bends away from the light.
The tip turns into a root.

question: Plant shoots are positively phototropic and negatively geotropic, whereas plant roots are negatively phototropic and positively geotropic.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: How do high concentrations of auxins (生長素) affect cell elongation in shoots versus roots?
options: High auxin concentrations stimulate elongation in both shoots and roots.
High auxin concentrations stimulate cell elongation in shoots, whereas the same high concentration inhibits cell elongation in roots.
Auxins have no effect on roots.
Auxins inhibit elongation in both shoots and roots.

question: When a young seedling is placed horizontally in the dark, why does its primary root bend downward (positive geotropism / 正向地性)?
options: Gravity pulls auxins to the upper side, causing faster growth on the lower side.
Auxins accumulate on the lower side due to gravity, inhibiting cell elongation on the lower side while the upper side elongates faster.
The root tip loses all water on the lower side.
Starch grains dissolve in the upper epidermis.

question: A clinostat (旋轉器) rotated slowly cancels out the unilateral effect of gravity on a horizontally placed seedling, causing its shoot and root to grow straight horizontally.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Why are rod cells (視桿細胞) more sensitive to dim light than cone cells?
options: Rod cells contain three types of colour-sensitive pigments.
Multiple rod cells share a single bipolar neurone (spatial summation) and contain visual purple (rhodopsin) that breaks down even in low light.
Rod cells are concentrated exclusively at the yellow spot.
Rod cells have larger nuclei than cone cells.

question: Which deficiency causes night blindness (夜盲症) due to impaired synthesis of visual purple in rod cells?
options: Vitamin C deficiency
Vitamin A deficiency / 缺乏維生素 A
Iron deficiency
Calcium deficiency

question: Colour blindness (色盲) is usually an inherited condition caused by the absence or defect of one or more types of cone cells on the retina.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: What is the survival advantage of positive phototropism in plant shoots?
options: It anchors the plant more deeply in soil.
It positions leaves toward maximum sunlight to maximize the rate of photosynthesis.
It prevents insects from landing on the petals.
It lowers the rate of transpiration to zero.
